questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Did the employer give the employee notice of termination of the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Did the employee make the compensation claim pending (German: "Klage anhängig gemacht") within 180 days of the end of the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Did the employee and the employer agree, after the notice, that the employment relationship would continue?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Did the employee lodge a written objection to the notice with the employer (German: "beim Kündigenden schriftlich Einsprache erheben") no later than the end of the notice period?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Did the employee ask the employer to state the reasons for the notice in writing?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Was the notice given because the employee had asserted, in good faith, claims arising from the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q7
questions.question: Has the notice period (from the notice to the end of the employment relationship) already ended?

questions.label: Q8
questions.question: Was the employee, when notice was given, an elected employee representative on the staff council of the business or on a body linked to the business?

questions.label: Q9
questions.question: Have more than 180 days passed since the employment relationship ended?

text:
Dear Sir or Madam

On 17 July 2026 I sent Seematt Management Ltd a registered letter objecting to my dismissal. I wrote that I don't accept it and want to keep my job, signed it, and kept the post office receipt. According to the tracking it was delivered to their office in Langenthal the next morning.

I'm a member of the staff committee there. My colleagues elected me in May 2023 and again last year, and I was on the committee when the notice came and still am. My colleague Kate Palmer, who chairs the committee, was shocked when I told her.

I'm still employed by Seematt for now, my job hasn't ended yet. I go in every day as usual. The notice period runs until the end of September, so there are still more than two months to go.

The notice itself was handed to me on 10 July 2026 by Owen Näf, the head of operations, in a short meeting in his office. It was a one-page letter ending my employment.

I earn CHF 2,990 a month and have been with the company since 2022. I'd like to understand what my objection means in practice and what I should do next while I'm still working there.

Kind regards
Liam Ellis
Mattenweg 23, Langenthal
